sections.content: How many people are "assemblers (vehicles and metal goods)"?

32,045 people

were counted on the census as "assemblers (vehicles and metal goods)" in England and Wales in March 2021.
Assemblers (vehicles and metal goods) undertake the routine assembly of vehicles and other metal goods or components such as frames, axles, wire brushes and wheels.

More men than women had this job

Among people working as "assemblers (vehicles and metal goods)" there were more men than women (83.5% compared with 16.5%).

This means "assemblers (vehicles and metal goods)" had a similar proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "process, plant and machine operatives".

Men made up 83.5% and women made up 16.5% of "assemblers (vehicles and metal goods)"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "assemblers (vehicles and metal goods)" included:

  • waste disposal and environmental services managers
  • engineering project managers and project engineers
  • plastics process operatives

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

People who had this job were generally similar in age to the working population

The occupation of "assemblers (vehicles and metal goods)" had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 30 to 34 years. Of the whole working population 12% were aged 30 to 34 years. For people working as "assemblers (vehicles and metal goods)", 14.4% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "assemblers (vehicles and metal goods)" was 16 to 19 years.

Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "assemblers (vehicles and metal goods)" included:

  • water and sewerage plant operatives
  • telecoms and related network installers and repairers
  • transport and distribution clerks and assistants

We can look at who worked as "assemblers (vehicles and metal goods)" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Men and women with this occupation had a similar age profile, as shown in the chart below.

The percentage of men and women who are "assemblers (vehicles and metal goods)" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "assemblers (vehicles and metal goods)", 7.8% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (95.7% compared with 4.3%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (98.4%) than self-employed (1.6%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the West Midlands. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Birmingham, this is in the same region of the West Midlands.
